mcp_handoff.note: Preview Surface approximates Blender materials; compare appearance in the target renderer.

checks.title: Missing files (textures, references, payloads, sublayers)
checks.why: A path that does not resolve loads nothing: a missing reference or payload drops geometry, and a missing texture renders as a flat or pink surface. URL paths (https://, omniverse://) cannot be checked offline and fail the same way when no resolver for them is installed.

checks.title: Composition errors (broken references and arcs)
checks.why: USD reported an arc it could not compose, so part of the asset is silently missing on the stage.

checks.title: Absolute file paths
checks.why: A path like C:/Users/me/asset/wood.png only works on the machine that wrote it. Move the folder or share it and every such file goes missing.

checks.title: Files outside the asset's folder
checks.why: The asset depends on files outside its own folder, so copying only that folder to a project, a teammate or a server leaves those files behind.

checks.title: Backslashes in asset paths
checks.why: Backslashes only work on Windows; Linux render farms and containers will not find the files.

checks.title: Units and up axis authored
checks.why: Without metersPerUnit and upAxis every tool guesses (USD's fallback is centimeters, Y up), so the asset can arrive 100x too big or lying on its side. Isaac Sim expects meters and Z up (Isaac validator profiles: MetersPerUnit1Checker, UpAxisZChecker).

checks.title: Unit or up-axis mismatch between files
checks.why: USD never rescales or rotates referenced data. A millimeter asset referenced into a meter stage appears 1000x too large; a Y-up asset in a Z-up stage lies on its back.

checks.title: defaultPrim set (here and in referenced files)
checks.why: defaultPrim tells a reference without a prim path which prim to bring in. A file without one references as empty unless every arc names the prim explicitly.

checks.title: Kind / model hierarchy
examples: Root prim /Asset contains geometry but has no kind.
checks.why: kind (component, assembly, group) lets tools treat the asset as one selectable model. A broken chain (a component inside a component, or a model under a prim without group/assembly) means model traversal and selection modes skip it.
how_to_fix: Give the asset root kind = component (a leaf asset) or assembly (an asset made of assets).
Every ancestor of a model must be group or assembly; parts inside a component use subcomponent or no kind.

checks.title: Extents present and up to date
checks.why: extent is a mesh's precomputed bounding box. Missing or stale extents make framing, culling and bounds queries wrong (objects vanish at some angles or 'frame selected' zooms to the wrong place).

checks.title: Mesh topology valid
checks.why: faceVertexCounts, faceVertexIndices and points disagree, so renderers drop or garble the mesh.

checks.title: Primvars (UVs, colors) sized and indexed correctly
checks.why: A primvar whose length or indices do not match its interpolation is ignored or reads garbage, so textures map wrongly.

checks.title: Normals sanity
checks.why: Normals decide smooth vs faceted shading. Wrong-length normals are ignored; normals on a subdivision mesh are ignored too (USD computes its own), which is why CAD/FBX imports often look blobby or faceted.

checks.title: Very heavy meshes
checks.why: A single mesh above 500,000 faces (or more than 10,000,000 faces in total) slows loading, selection and physics; CAD tessellation is the usual cause.

checks.title: Repeated geometry not instanced
checks.why: Many copies of the same asset or identical meshes each cost memory and load time. Marking references instanceable lets USD share one prototype across all copies.

checks.title: Instancing set up correctly
checks.why: instanceable without a composition arc does nothing, and edits below an instance are ignored.

checks.title: Every visible mesh has a material
checks.why: An unbound mesh renders with the renderer's default grey; a binding to a missing material or one outside the referenced asset is silently dropped.

checks.title: Materials have a surface shader
checks.why: A Material whose outputs:surface (or outputs:mdl:surface) connects to nothing renders as if unbound.

checks.title: Shading models used (UsdPreviewSurface / MDL / MaterialX)
checks.why: MDL looks best in Omniverse RTX but other tools (Blender, usdview) show only UsdPreviewSurface. Assets meant to travel should carry a UsdPreviewSurface too.
how_to_fix: Nothing to fix; this is information. For portability add a UsdPreviewSurface network next to the MDL.

checks.title: Texture formats, sizes and color spaces
checks.why: Only PNG, JPEG and EXR load everywhere. Normal, roughness, metallic and AO maps hold data, not color, and must be read as 'raw'; read as sRGB they shade wrongly. Very large textures cost GPU memory.

checks.title: Prim names portable
checks.why: Non-ASCII or very long prim names (common from CAD part numbers) break older tools, scripts and some Isaac/ROS pipelines.

checks.title: Empty Xforms
checks.why: Xforms with no children are often leftovers from an exporter (null nodes, empty groups). They do no harm but clutter the tree.

checks.title: Hierarchy depth
checks.why: Trees deeper than 24 levels (typical of CAD assemblies) make the stage slow to traverse and hard to navigate.

checks.title: Time samples on static content
checks.why: Values written as time samples that never change (often one sample at frame 0 from an exporter) make tools treat the asset as animated, which disables caching and can hide default values.

checks.title: Colliders on heavy render meshes
checks.why: Using a render mesh with more than 20,000 faces as a triangle-mesh collider makes physics slow, and moving rigid bodies cannot simulate triangle meshes at all (PhysX falls back to a convex hull).

checks.title: Rigid bodies with explicit mass
checks.why: A rigid body without MassAPI gets its mass from collider volume times a default density (1000 kg/m3, water), which is often far from the real part and makes robots and grippers behave oddly.
